item.title: EPIC: Differentiable Energy-Force Consistent Uncertainty Quantification and Propagation for Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
item.description: arXiv:2611.00942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) now rival density functional theory in accuracy and are increasingly used to screen vast crystal databases, yet they can produce unreliable predictions for chemistries outside their training distribution without clear warning. Existing force-level evidential approaches do not inherently define a corresponding uncertainty model over the potential energy surface, limiting the consistent propagation of uncertainty to energy-derived observables. Here we introduce Energy-Propagated Intrinsic Confidence (EPIC), a general energy-centered evidential framework that derives forces as exact gradients of the predicted mean energy, ensuring conservative force fields while providing an analytical estimate of energy uncertainty. Coupled to a MACE backbone trained on the Materials Project trajectory dataset, EPIC propagates uncertainty diagnostics to equations of state, anisotropic structural uncertainty ellipsoids, and phonon dispersions through a Monte Carlo procedure. Applied to 10,966 candidate crystals, the fraction classified as robustly dynamically stable increases from 11\% in the highest-uncertainty quartile to 53\% in the lowest-uncertainty quartile. Furthermore, element-resolved analysis reveals a pronounced chemistry dependence in the relationship between epistemic uncertainty and predicted dynamical stability, highlighting potential limitations in the description of complex bonding environments. EPIC thus provides a physics-aware, chemistry-sensitive uncertainty diagnostic for high-throughput screening and autonomous materials discovery.
item.dc:creator: Tianhao Su, Musen Li, Shunbo Hu, Tong-Yi Zhang

item.title: Learned Warm Starts for Steady Transonic RANS Simulations of Wing and Aircraft Configurations
item.description: arXiv:2611.01240v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural surrogates can accelerate many-query aerodynamic analyses, but their standalone predictions may be insufficiently accurate or robust to support reliable design evaluations. We develop a learned warm-start formulation that predicts mean-flow and turbulence fields directly on native CFD meshes for subsequent correction by the RANS solver. A common architecture and objective structure are used across subcritical and transonic flows, including challenging conditions with shock-induced separation. A condition-modulated Transolver combines Fourier and wall features with target-gated regularization, a Sobolev-type loss, adaptive loss weighting and sampled training. Prediction requires no preliminary flow solution, and training requires no solver-residual evaluation. Extensive 3D CFD evaluations on SuperWing, the NASA Common Research Model (CRM) and DLR-F6 assess geometric and operating-condition generalization, including interpolation, extrapolation and cross-mesh deployment, using Spalart-Allmaras and $k$-$\omega$ SST closures on million-cell meshes. Unseen nominal cases achieve geometric-mean iteration speed-ups of approximately $2$-$4\times$ under a common convergence criterion based on cold-run aerodynamic coefficients. On CRM, learned initialization provides greater aggregate acceleration than nearest-condition restarts using the same solution library. Resolution invariance enables direct deployment of coarse-mesh models on finer meshes without retraining, solution interpolation or target-condition coarse solves. Including data generation and training, estimated campaign speed-ups reach $2.1$-$2.3\times$. No warm run diverges; fewer than $2\%$ fail to satisfy the cold-reference convergence criterion. These results support learned initialization for repeated aerodynamic analyses, while highlighting initialization sensitivity near separation as a remaining limitation.
item.dc:creator: Muhammad Irfan Zafar, Saleh Abuhanieh, \c{S}ahin Yi\u{g}it

item.title: Learning structural response operators across varying geometries and loads with global and local geometry encoding
item.description: arXiv:2611.01861v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Predicting mechanical responses across complex geometries and varying loading conditions is central to simulation-driven engineering, yet capturing the influence of geometric boundaries remains challenging for data-driven models. Here we propose a Load- and Geometry-adaptive Deep Operator Network (LG-DON) that integrates global geometric representations with local, boundary-aware information to predict structural responses. By distinguishing distances to different boundary categories rather than relying on the nearest boundary alone, the framework captures spatially varying geometric influences that conventional distance-based representations may overlook. Across benchmark problems involving diverse non-convex geometries, LG-DON reduces the mean relative L2 error from 12.17% for a modified MIONet baseline to 7.41%. Controlled ablation studies further demonstrate the advantages of category-resolved boundary distances and show that combining global and local geometric representations outperforms either representation alone in 15 of 18 evaluated configurations. These findings highlight the value of integrating complementary geometric information for accurate operator learning across complex structural domains.
item.dc:creator: Xin Liu, Wuwen Yao

item.title: The Cryptocurrency Trend Factor Revisited: Predictive Information, Portfolio Construction, and Pricing Claims
item.description: arXiv:2611.01951v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We reassess five economic claims about the cryptocurrency trend factor (CTREND): cross-sectional return predictability, high risk-adjusted performance, incremental information beyond market, size, and momentum, the ability to replace momentum in factor models, and robustness among large and liquid coins and after trading costs. Our reconstruction and code audit identify issues in information timing, technical indicators, forecast coverage, portfolio formation, and return accounting. We first correct future-information use and related settlement rules, then implement broader corrections to indicators, forecast availability, and portfolio accounting. Without additional coin exclusions, the first stage changes CTREND's mean weekly gross return from 4.07% to 4.25%, annualized Sharpe ratio from 2.08 to 1.48, and weekly alpha relative to published market, size, and momentum factors from 2.77% to 3.06%. After comprehensive correction, these become 0.05%, 0.01, and -1.38%; the alpha is no longer significant. Replacing momentum with CTREND yields an advantage in maximum squared Sharpe ratios of 0.058 in the original implementation, 0.024 after the first-stage correction, and -0.0185 after comprehensive correction, with a statistically significant overall decline. Mean weekly gross returns for the largest 100 coins change from 2.93% to 3.99% to 1.00%, while mean weekly net returns for the full long-short portfolio under the lowest assumed trading costs change from 2.93% to 3.35% to -0.87%. These findings show that reported performance and factor-substitution gains depend materially on implementation and sample composition. We distinguish predictive information, an independent return premium, and the incremental value of replacing an existing factor as separate economic claims.
item.dc:creator: Yifei Wang, Zhenling Pang

item.title: Allen--Cahn Residual-Constrained Topology Optimization via an Augmented Lagrangian Method
item.description: arXiv:2611.02375v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a residual-constrained topology optimization framework that controls interface transition bandwidth without requiring external density filters. The steady conserved Allen--Cahn (AC) equation is formulated as an equality residual constraint and solved via a mass-weighted Augmented Lagrangian Method (ALM) coupled with the Method of Moving Asymptotes (MMA). A closed-form chemical potential projection eliminates the constant residual mode, ensuring algebraic compatibility with external volume targets. Variational sensitivity analysis reveals a symmetric-plus-rank-one Jacobian that yields matrix-free sensitivities without additional adjoint PDE solves, reducing residual sensitivity overhead to only 0.11% of the state elasticity solve time in 3D. Systematic 2D benchmarks confirm that interface bandwidth is governed intrinsically by reaction--diffusion parameters across mesh refinements. While diffuse interfaces incur a continuous compliance elevation (1.4%--12.3%), a volume-preserving 0/1 post-processing audit across 48 benchmark cases demonstrates that this gap stems primarily from intermediate-density penalization: binarized AC-ALM designs achieve equal or superior stiffness in 45 configurations (averaging 1.2% stiffer than SIMP). Simultaneously, single-node hinges and strut fragmentation are substantially suppressed compared to unregularized baselines. Three-dimensional benchmarks further demonstrate practical spatial viability for complex structures.
item.dc:creator: Run Du, Xuan Xiao, Wenming Cheng, Zeqiang Zhang

item.title: AMLBench: A Real-Incident Benchmark for Agentic Blockchain Anti-Money Laundering
item.description: arXiv:2611.02530v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tracing illicit funds on public blockchains remains largely manual. As funds move across accounts and undergo asset conversions, they become mixed with other inflows, requiring repeated queries and expert judgment to trace. Large language model (LLM) agents offer a way to automate this process, but their ability to reconstruct case-related transfer networks from limited clues remains unclear. To bridge this gap, we present AMLBench, an anti-money laundering (AML) benchmark built from 24 real-world cases and 5.05 million Ethereum transfer records. For each case, agents start from limited clues and explore these transfer records through composable transaction-query and fund-flow analysis tools, deciding which accounts and branches to pursue. The final tracing results are evaluated against case annotations, while tool interaction logs reveal how agents discover and select relevant transfers and at what resource cost. We also develop AMLAgent, which integrates fund-tracing guidance and query feedback to dynamically guide investigative decisions. With GPT-6 Astra, AMLAgent achieves macro averages of 80.82% transfer-level precision and 84.73% query coverage across 24 real-world cases. Further analysis of the large-scale Bybit case reveals substantial differences in transfer retention and token usage across models, even with similar submission precision. AMLBench establishes a reproducible benchmark for evaluating both tracing outcomes and investigative processes, laying the groundwork for more reliable and efficient autonomous AML investigations.
item.dc:creator: Qishuang Fu, Hang Zheng, Yuchen Lei, Yuexin Xiang, Qin Wang, Yuanzhe Zhang, Shiping Chen, Andreas Deppeler, Joseph Liu, Ziyao Liu, Tsz Hon Yuen

item.title: Herding or Racing? Decomposing Cross-Account Order-Flow Persistence in On-Chain Markets
item.description: arXiv:2611.02616v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Most of the autocorrelation in trade signs on decentralized exchanges comes from pairs of trades sent by different wallets. For Uniswap v3, this has been read as herding dominating order splitting -- the reverse of what equity markets show. We show that this herding share mixes two quantities: the probability $p$ that consecutive orders come from the same account, which is small when thousands of wallets are trading, and the ratio $\kappa$ of cross-account to same-account sign correlation. For any $p$, $\kappa$ equals one under the public-signal benchmark of T\'oth et al. and zero under independent order splitting. On Uniswap v3 USDC-WETH (one week each in 2023 and 2024), the herding share is 0.65-0.86, but $\kappa$ is only 0.05-0.10. On a fully on-chain EVM limit order book, the herding share is similar (0.61-0.87), but $\kappa$ is 0.72-0.76; among Uniswap swaps above USD 100k, it is 0.34-0.52. Where $\kappa$ is high, cross-account co-movement is mostly a race for the price on a centralized exchange. It is concentrated in orders a few blocks apart, and a cross-fitted gradient-boosted filter that sees only Binance data removes about three quarters or more of it. This race flow accounts for most of the losses of liquidity providers. We recommend reporting $\kappa$ alongside the herding share and modeling on-chain order flow as splitting traders plus arbitrageurs who respond to the centralized-exchange price.
item.dc:creator: Yichong Bai (The Hong Kong Polytechnic University), Dingyue Kan (The Hong Kong Polytechnic University)

item.title: Green Composites for Safer and Durable Water Pipelines
item.description: arXiv:2611.02837v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The intensifying water shortage in Algeria makes clear the need of novel, sustainable strategies to protect distribution networks. Current infrastructure struggles with frequent failures, particularly leaks stemming from corrosion or handling damage during transport and installation. High-density polyethylene (HDPE) has become a material of choice because it handles these challenges well; it is cost-efficient, flexible, and tough enough to withstand harsh environments.This work investigates the failure risks of HDPE pipelines manufactured by ITP Alg{\'e}rie -- Innovation Transformation Polym{\`e}re. Mechanical tests were performed on HDPE 100 to determine its fundamental properties, including burst tests under internal pressure and load/unload experiments aimed at establishing a material-specific damage law revealed the dominant degradation mechanisms that occur under different operational and environmental conditions. Based on these findings, a predictive numerical model was developed to simulate damage progression and anticipate potential failures in service. This study introduces a unique hybrid composite patch designed for the precise rehabilitation of compromised pipeline sections. It shows strong promise for rebuilding the mechanical integrity of pipes, which is vital for maintaining a safe and long-lasting drinking water supply.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: WSEAS Transactions on Environment and Development, 2026, 23, pp.1
item.dc:creator: Djebbara Benzerga (USTO MB), Faycal Sotehi (USTO MB), Adel Chouiter (UA), Abdelkader Haddi (UA), Nahla Benzerga

item.title: Inner optimizers in active-learning Kriging reliability analysis: a pre-specified comparison and the unconservative estimates left by unlearned failure modes
item.description: arXiv:2611.03117v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Active-learning Kriging often replaces candidate pools by continuous metaheuristic search. A pre-specified comparison sharing surrogate, population and stopping rule isolated this inner optimizer: five budget-matched continuous optimizers, including hybrid swarm optimization with L-BFGS-B polishing, against candidate pools on eleven problems (dimension 2 to 100). The primary hypothesis was not supported: against optimizers sharing its criterion the hybrid won 6, tied 41 and lost 19 of 66 Holm-corrected accuracy comparisons, and against pool methods 0, 23 and 21 of 44. With sequential selection on three series systems, multistart L-BFGS-B left a failure mode unlearned in 59 of 60 runs, more often than swarm, genetic-algorithm or AK-MCS. In all 198 runs (22 post-freeze) with an unlearned mode, the learned modes did not compensate and failure probability was underestimated (exploratory). The error criterion can accept substantial underestimation: it accepted 17 runs (13 pool-selected) at 0.38 to 0.89 of the reference; 181 exhausted the budget. Follow-up analyses on single-design-point problems indicate underestimation when selections concentrate near the design point. Kriging-believer pool selection satisfied the surrogate stopping criterion with fewer calls than the best continuous method in all four informative batch cells (two post-freeze). We recommend default pool selection and coverage checks for any selection.
item.dc:creator: Wei-Chang Yeh

item.title: DiffStent: Surrogate Adjoint Differentiation for Stent Deployment in Anisotropic Arteries
item.description: arXiv:2611.00014v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present DiffStent, a differentiable finite element framework for simulating arterial deformation during in silico stent deployment, where nearly incompressible, anisotropic vessel walls undergo large deformation and frictional contact with the stent. DiffStent combines the fiber-reinforced Holzapfel-Gasser-Ogden constitutive model with an implicit discrete adjoint that differentiates the converged mechanical equilibrium without unrolling the nonlinear solver, thus reducing the memory cost by three orders of magnitude. We identify three mechanisms that can lead to inaccurate, unstable, or uninformative gradients: nonsmooth switching, state mismatch, and gradient cancellation. To address these, we apply a contact surrogate in the backward pass while retaining the original physical model in the forward pass. We show superior gradient accuracy of our method over AutoDiff and finite differencing across constitutive benchmarks, idealized stented vessels, and patient-specific calcified coronary anatomies, and use the resulting sensitivities to quantify how tissue properties and calcification patterns govern lumen expansion and arterial wall stress. Finally, we demonstrate that DiffStent enables gradient-based system identification from retrospective clinical images of atherosclerotic coronary anatomy. Together, these results establish a practical approach for differentiating through nonlinear biomechanical simulations with stiff constitutive laws and nonsmooth contact, enabling patient-specific parameter inference and optimization in computational cardiovascular mechanics.
item.dc:creator: Shoaib A. Goraya, Ajay Manicka, Aviral Jain, Karim Kadry, Samuel Ruiperez-Campillo, Elazer R. Edelman, Farhad R. Nezami

item.title: Excel: A Financial Modelling System
item.description: arXiv:2611.00164v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Since the calculation engine of Excel was the subject of a major upgrade to accommodate Dynamic Arrays in 2018, there has been a series of seismic changes to the art of financial modelling. This paper will show the traditional financial modelling techniques for spreadsheets can be replaced by radically different approaches that have significant gains in readability, performance and flexibility. With so much power added to the Excel engine in recent years, it is the responsibility of financial modellers to ensure that they are building in the simplest and most auditable way possible going forward.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Proceedings of the EuSpRIG 2026 conference 'Spreadsheets, AI Agents, Trust, and Governance' ISBN 9781-905404-61-2 1-905404-61-2 Copyright 2026, European Spreadsheet Risks Interest Group and Authors

item.title: GURU: A Hierarchical Neuro-Symbolic Multi-Agent System for Verification-Aware Automation of Mission-Critical Digital Engineering and Operations
item.description: arXiv:2611.01001v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An AI can find a safe action faster than any human, but it must never decide what counts as safe. We present GURU, a hierarchical neuro-symbolic multi-agent system for mission-critical digital engineering and operations, built on one partition of authority: learned models propose, rank, and accelerate; a symbolic rules engine checks every consequential action against hard limits before it executes; and validated physics confirms and decides. GURU runs a workflow as a closed control loop, with Navigation, Action, and Planning agents sharing one Common Internal Language and one training factory. Nuclear, aviation, and national-security guidance now requires this pattern; a harnessed language model keeps the model at the center, GURU puts a validated reference there. In computational fluid dynamics, the workflow raised the converged-simulation rate on unseen aircraft geometries from under 1 percent to 74 percent over 100 single-attempt cases, ran 54 live cases to Mach 6 on three facilities, and an ablation put the symbolic layer at 13 points of boundary-layer capture. Knowledge-graph retrieval and role adapters raised ParaView control success from 55 to 75 percent. In space domain awareness, where a language model cannot be trusted to decide, a frozen self-supervised world model under validated propagation scored highest of five methods at conjunction risk, including fully fine-tuned language models, with several-times-lower seed variance: the trustworthy design gives up nothing in accuracy, and the recipe transferred to reactor anomaly detection. A radar-to-avoidance debris pipeline was demonstrated in stages on a 2026 reentry; the hierarchy coordinates simulated teams of 200 aircraft. Training scaled near-linearly past 1,000 Aurora nodes and ran at 8,000. The approach extends to a control-grade microreactor digital twin with validated physics, not a learned model, as the safety basis.
item.dc:creator: Allan Grosvenor, Anton Zemlyansky, Abdul Wahab, Kyrylo Bohachov, Aras Dogan, Ryland Adams, Dwyer Deighan

item.title: AIDA: An AI Outage Registry with Evidence from On-Chain MEV
item.description: arXiv:2611.01656v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative AI coding tools have lowered the cost of writing trading software, but no systematic dataset records when these services fail. We introduce the AI Incident and Disruption Archive (AIDA), a multi-vendor registry of 5,868 deduplicated outage incidents across 30 providers from 2025 to 2026, with foundation-model incidents verified against primary status-page or postmortem URLs. Pairing AIDA with 5,041,034 verified maximal extractable value (MEV) transactions by 8,516 Ethereum addresses, their contract creations, and a 22-month Base Layer-2 panel of 1,099,593,191 swaps and 29,120 private executors, we establish two findings. First, entry into MEV expanded where code and public state suffice, as active arbitrage addresses quadrupled from late 2024 to late 2026 and liquidators grew by a third, while sandwich attackers, who need private order flow and builder access, declined. Execution nonetheless remained concentrated, with the top fifty addresses executing two thirds of verified trades. Second, AI outages stall new trading code while deployed bots keep trading. On Ethereum, addresses releasing a private executor fall to 0.67 on the day of an eight-hour disruption (0.68 for executor creations during OpenAI outage hours) and to 0.66 at lag two before rebounding on day three; on Base, operator top-level creations fall to 0.76 during OpenAI hours and executor-deploying operators to 0.88 at lag two. Non-trading creations, automated factory clones, and live arbitrage and sandwich execution across both chains remain unchanged. Cheaper code thus lowers the barrier to building MEV contracts, while private order flow, latency and capital still determine who wins execution.
item.dc:creator: Wenbin Wu

item.title: Long-term yields of short-rate models as Feynman-Kac ground states: a variational quantum eigensolver with single-setting energy estimation on two NISQ platforms
item.description: arXiv:2611.01855v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that the long-term yield of a short-rate model is the ground-state energy of a Schrodinger operator obtained from the Feynman-Kac bond-pricing equation, so that it can be computed by a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE). We treat the Vasicek, Cox-Ingersoll-Ross and Black-Karasinski models; the last has no closed form. Calibrated monthly to the U.S. Treasury curve from 1985 to 2026, the long-term yield follows the 30-year yield with an in-sample correlation of 0.98. The Hamiltonian is stoquastic, so its ground state is positive and the energy can be estimated from computational-basis samples with a single measurement setting. On ibm_cleveland, gate noise appears mainly as bit flips of the high-order qubits. A bit-flip deconvolution with a tail set fixed by a WKB criterion, combined with readout mitigation and zero-noise extrapolation, gives four-qubit estimates within 33-125 bp of the grid ground-state energies for all three models, and within 23-67 bp for Treasury-calibrated parameters. On IonQ Forte Enterprise the same analysis reduces the error in the same proportions. On the same circuits, a Pauli-measurement VQE deviates by 791-1,129 bp, so the single-setting estimator gives about ten times smaller errors with one setting instead of nine. An on-device VQE converges from 4,939 bp to 130 bp.
item.dc:creator: Doyeol "David" Ahn (Department of Electrical,Computer Engineering, University of Seoul, Seoul 02504, Republic of Korea,,Singularity Quantum Inc., Newport Beach, CA 92660, USA)

item.title: Parameterisation of NMC and LFP 4680 cells for electrochemical and thermal modelling
item.description: arXiv:2611.01938v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An electrochemical-thermal model of the 4680 cylindrical cell is presented: a Doyle-Fuller-Newman model of the electrode stack coupled to a two-node thermal balance of the roll and the can (a thermal DFN, TDFN), solved by an implicit finite-volume scheme. Two cells are parameterised from teardown geometry and open literature, with every value tagged by provenance: the Tesla NMC811/graphite tabless cell and the BYD FC4680 LiFePO4 multi-tab cell. The reaction heat is evaluated at the open-circuit potential of the particle-mean concentration, which restores the heat of mixing. Both sets are calibrated in the same way, with the test fixture identified from the measurement alone. Against the 1C and 2C charge test of Ank et al., the calibrated NMC set follows the mean can temperature within 0.52 and 1.46 K, with a contact heat of 0.94 mOhm matching the authors' estimate for their holder. For the LFP cell, 1C and 2C discharges to 2.0 V were measured on the authors' bench; the fixture conductance (0.337 W/K) follows from the energy balance and the heat capacity (277 J/K) from the cooling. With the end-of-lithiation drop of LiFePO4 restored in the cathode open-circuit potential, the calibrated set follows the can temperature within 0.44 K (1C) and 0.76 K (2C), reproduces the peaks and the relaxation after cut-off. What remains is what a single can node and a single representative particle do not describe: the axial gradient of the NMC can under contact heating, and a gradual decline of the LFP voltage before the knee at 2C, which points to the distribution of particle states in the electrode. The parameter sets (BPX, CSV) and the bench data are openly available.
item.dc:creator: Remus Teodorescu, Nicolai A. Weinreich, Berke Bilgin, Yi Zhuang, Wenzel Prochazka

item.title: Data-driven candidate structure ensemble generation beyond the convex hull with crystALL approach
item.description: arXiv:2611.02584v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Real materials consist of multiple stable or metastable states under real-world conditions, existing as statistical ergodic ensembles of configurations rather than ideal crystals. Yet, data-driven computational materials discovery increasingly biases itself toward finding "new stable structures" from ground-state DFT calculations alone. This limits our long-term ability to discover materials whose properties emerge from metastable phases, to explain experimental observations, or to model thermodynamic behavior comprehensively. Predicting ergodic sets of atomic configurations of known and hypothetical solids is a fundamental challenge in theoretical crystallography, approached via many complementary methods. We discuss this conceptually and introduce crystALL, a pragmatic and powerful data-driven approach to discovering ensembles beyond the convex hull, embracing structural diversity over stability alone, enabling robust experiment matching in cases evading traditional methods. crystALL leverages 5 million relaxed structures from OPTIMADE and MPDD to rapidly generate a comprehensive candidate set by: (1) species substitutions; (2) ML feature-space analysis with pySIPFENN; (3) representative structure selection via clustering and energy-minimization or property matching; and (4) construction of the final candidate ensemble for experimental or ab initio validation. We also uniquely address the common challenge of experimental composition uncertainties spanning many integer stoichiometries by new efficient searches across anonymized compositional ranges rather than fixed formulas. Overall, crystALL's ensemble-focused philosophy provides critical advantages over the prevailing convex-hull-searching paradigm, which often fails to account for key experimental observations and increases AI/ML discovery bias over time - akin to model collapse in LLMs retrained on iteratively generated content.
item.dc:creator: Adam M. Krajewski, Ricardo Amaral, Jonathan W. Siegel, Luke A. Myers, Rushi Gong, Shun-Li Shang, Zi-Kui Liu

item.title: Interpretable Allocation and Model-Predictive Rebalancing of Equity Portfolios, Tested on Real and Synthetic Markets
item.description: arXiv:2611.03022v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A live equity portfolio poses three problems: which stocks to hold, when to trade, and whether the strategy holds up beyond the observed market. We built one system for all three and tested it on 373 US equities, calibrated on 2014-2024 and traded from January 2025 to September 2026. A selection rule chose stocks by score, by a bandit, or at random, and one of seven weighting rules, four consumer-theory utilities, and three standard portfolios, set share counts under limits on budget, single-stock weight, portfolio volatility, and turnover, with each stock's preference weight a bounded score of its trend, market beta, and the market's recent direction. A model-predictive controller forecasts portfolio value with a multi-asset geometric Brownian motion and re-planned at its horizon, when the value left its forecast band, or at a drawdown stop. To probe deeper declines than the real window held, we also ran the system on simulated markets from per-asset hidden Markov generators with jumps, linked by market and sector factors. On real prices, the stocks chosen mattered more to terminal wealth than the weighting rule, and the early re-plans shrank the worst drawdown in most rule combinations against a fixed calendar without consistently raising wealth. In the deepest simulated declines, every combination, random picks included, ended above simulated SPY and the equal-weight universe in the median, even without early re-plans, so the margin came from shared parts of the system, not from stock selection or re-plan timing. A market hedge that tightened a beta cap as the market weakened cost wealth on real prices but paid off in the most sustained simulated declines, and the generator's persistent trends favored score-based selection more than the real market did, which suggests a synthetic test judges stock selection fairly only if its generator does not build in that persistence.
item.dc:creator: Jeffrey D. Varner

item.title: PaddleMaterials: An End-to-End Deep Learning Toolkit for Materials Science
item.description: arXiv:2611.03154v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Machine learning supports materials design, atomistic simulation and experimental characterization, yet models and workflows remain fragmented. We present PaddleMaterials, an open-source framework integrating heterogeneous materials-learning tasks while preserving task-specific representations and scientific semantics. It unifies data processing, training, evaluation, pretrained-model management and workflows across six task classes: property prediction, structure generation, machine-learning interatomic potentials, electronic-structure fields, spectrum elucidation and microscopy image processing. Task interfaces record physical quantities, units, aggregation conventions and references, making cross-task composition verifiable. A shared compiler backend enables switching from dynamic-graph to compiled execution through one setting, using graph optimization, operator fusion and hardware-targeted code generation without changing model definitions. Across 65 model instances in 11 groups, compiled execution accelerated every instance in eight groups, with group median speedups of 11%-224% and group maximum speedups of 11%-336%. Case studies on LiMnO2 and toluene link structure generation or spectrum elucidation, interatomic-potential relaxation, property prediction and electron-density prediction, using same-geometry density functional theory (DFT) calculations as references. For LiMnO2, predicted formation energies for generated and relaxed structures differed from same-geometry PBE+U references by at most 7 meV per atom, while the computational cost of model steps was less than one-twentieth of a DFT single-point calculation. PaddleMaterials extends unified materials workflows beyond conventional property, potential and structure-generation tasks while supporting verifiable cross-task operations and compiled execution.
item.dc:creator: Xuwei Liu, Zhimin Zhang, Xiaoguang Hu, Zhongwei Liu, Yuanhui Sun, Jun Huo, Hua Wu, Haifeng Wang

item.title: Fracture-Bench: A Controlled Benchmark Suite for Machine Learning Surrogates in Phase-Field Fracture Mechanics
item.description: arXiv:2611.03473v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Machine-learning surrogates are increasingly proposed to replace phase-field fracture simulations in many-query tasks such as uncertainty quantification, inverse analysis and design. Little controlled evidence shows which architectures are reliable, for which fracture problems and how far beyond their training data. We introduce Fracture-Bench, an open benchmark of two phase-field datasets with fixed splits, common test metrics and a description of each dataset's physical regime. Dataset~1 contains 1,000 AT2 simulations of multiple cracks growing from a notched hole in a hyperelastic plate under random non-uniform biaxial boundary displacements (44 load steps, $128\times128$ grid). Dataset~2 contains 4,000 PF-CZM simulations of a pre-cracked plate with two inclusions, each ten times stiffer or more compliant than the matrix ($128\times256$ grid). We train a Fourier neural operator (FNO), DeepONet, Latent DeepONet, a UNet and a conditional diffusion model on identical splits and compare one test metric per dataset, training time, inference time and model size. On Dataset~1, FNO and Latent DeepONet attain mean test errors of order $10^{-6}$, about ten times lower than UNet and DeepONet. On Dataset~2, the diffusion model is most accurate, with about one sixth of the UNet error, but requires \SI{706}{s} per prediction versus \SI{6}{ms} for UNet. For all architectures, most of the error occurs in the final load steps, after crack localization. Dataset~2 contains initial cracks less than one grid cell apart that produce qualitatively different paths. Architecture rankings therefore depend on the task, and errors averaged over densely sampled inputs reveal little about near-bifurcation cases. Data, codes, splits, regime descriptors and generalization splits are public, with a protocol for adding under-represented regimes such as mixed-mode, three-dimensional and experimentally paired fracture.
item.dc:creator: Meenu Krishnan U., Maryam Hakimzadeh, Indrashish Saha, Meer Mehran Rashid, Lori Graham-Brady, Somdatta Goswami

item.title: 3D-BBDA: Backpropagation-Free Black-Box Domain Adaptation for Robust 3D Point Cloud Recognition
item.description: arXiv:2611.03588v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Robust 3D point-cloud recognition is critical for robotics, mapping, and urban sensing, yet point-cloud classifiers often suffer performance drops under domain shifts caused by sensor changes, environmental variation, and acquisition artifacts. Many existing adaptation methods are difficult to deploy in practice because they require access to source data or the internal parameters of the source model, which may be restricted by privacy, licensing, or security constraints. We present 3D-BBDA, a backpropagation-free black-box domain adaptation framework that adapts a source-trained predictor to unlabeled target data using only black-box outputs. Our method performs pseudo-label guided prototype-based alignment and employs a weighted prediction module to fuse source logits with alignment logits, reducing sensitivity to noisy pseudo-labels. To stabilize prototype memory when pseudo-label coverage is incomplete, we construct a Gaussian-perturbed prototype prior from unlabeled target predictions and use it as a fallback for missing or unreliable class prototypes during alignment. Experiments on four corrupted 3D benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over strong baselines. On ModelNet-40C, 3D-BBDA achieves mean errors of 32.08% (PointNet) and 29.62% (GDANet), outperforming Source-only (35.88% / 34.03%) and BFTT3D (33.78% / 32.36%). 3D-BBDA requires only a single forward pass with no gradient updates making it suitable for real-time, privacy-preserving deployment in transferable 3D recognition pipelines. Project page is available at https://visdomlab.github.io/3D_BBDA
item.dc:creator: Shivangi Rai, Kunal Jangid, Vaibhav Kumar, Vinod K Kurmi

item.title: Using Local Large Language Models to Build Reproducible and Differentiable ODE Parameter Estimation Pipelines
item.description: arXiv:2509.07283v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Parameter estimation for ordinary differential equation (ODE) models requires a sequence of interconnected tasks, including implementing model equations, mapping simulated quantities to experimental observations, constructing objective functions, configuring numerical solvers, and assessing fitted results. This chapter presents an agentic workflow that uses locally deployed large language models (LLMs) to assist with these tasks while retaining human oversight of scientific decisions. The workflow divides the estimation process into focused stages, each supplied with task-specific instructions and subject to validation before proceeding. Starting from a mathematical problem description and experimental data, it generates a structured configuration, a readable model implementation, and differentiable code for numerical optimization. Population-based global search is followed by gradient-based refinement using automatic differentiation through the ODE solution. Post-fit diagnostics examine residuals, optimization behavior, and local parameter sensitivity, while preserved intermediate artifacts allow users to inspect assumptions and revisit individual stages. A worked example demonstrates the complete procedure, and additional examples illustrate its application to diverse dynamical systems. The chapter provides a practical approach to constructing and revising ODE parameter-estimation pipelines in locally managed computing environments.
item.dc:creator: Saakaar Bhatnagar

item.title: Capsule Network-Based Multimodal Fusion for Mortgage Risk Assessment from Unstructured Data Sources
item.description: arXiv:2510.22987v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Mortgage risk assessment traditionally relies on structured financial data, which is often proprietary, confidential, and costly. In this study, we propose a novel multimodal deep learning framework that uses cost-free, publicly available, unstructured data sources, including textual information, images, and sentiment scores, to generate credit scores that approximate commercial scorecards. Our framework adopts a two-phase approach. In the unimodal phase, we identify the best-performing models for each modality, i.e. BERT for text, VGG for image data, and a multilayer perceptron for sentiment-based features. In the fusion phase, we introduce the capsule-based fusion network (FusionCapsNet), a novel fusion strategy inspired by capsule networks, but fundamentally redesigned for multimodal integration. Unlike standard capsule networks, our method adapts a specific mechanism in capsule networks to each modality and restructures the fusion process to preserve spatial, contextual, and modality-specific information. It also enables adaptive weighting so that stronger modalities dominate without ignoring complementary signals. Our framework incorporates sentiment analysis across distinct news categories to capture borrower and market dynamics and employs GradCAM-based visualizations as an interpretability tool. These components are designed features of the framework, while our results later demonstrate that they effectively enrich contextual understanding and highlight the influential factors driving mortgage risk predictions. Our results show that our multimodal FusionCapsNet framework not only exceeds individual unimodal models but also outperforms benchmark fusion strategies such as addition, concatenation, and cross attention in terms of AUC, partial AUC, and F1 score, demonstrating clear gains in both predictive accuracy and interpretability for mortgage risk assessment.
item.dc:creator: Mahsa Tavakoli, Rohitash Chandra, Cristian Bravo

item.title: In-context learning as a retraining-free paradigm for constitutive modeling
item.description: arXiv:2604.23098v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Building models that generalize across physical systems without retraining remains a central challenge in computational science. Here we introduce In-Context Modeling (ICM), a retrain-free paradigm that infers physical relationships directly from observational fields. Rather than encoding system-specific behavior in fixed parameters, ICM assimilates measurements as physical context and performs inference through a single forward pass. Trained in a physics-informed, label-free manner using governing equations, a single model generalizes across unseen materials, geometries, and loading conditions. Demonstrated on hyperelasticity, ICM integrates with finite-element simulations and is validated using experimental full-field measurements. Moreover, performance improves with increasing data diversity and computational budget, exhibiting favorable scaling behavior analogous to foundation models. By recasting physical modeling as in-context inference, this work establishes a transferable paradigm for retrain-free scientific learning and a foundation for scalable modeling across computational science.
item.dc:creator: Lingfeng Li, Zhuoyuan Li, Shun Li, Kaixin Zhan, Huajian Gao, Changqing Chen, Liu Yang

item.title: Data-free neural PDE solvers based on Graph Neural Networks and weak forms
item.description: arXiv:2607.27901v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a physics-informed, data-free neural solver for partial differential equations, built on a graph neural network architecture that utilises message passing. By relying on the weak form of the problem, we use gradients of finite-element shape functions (which are therefore polynomials) rather than automatic differentiation operators to compute the residuals of the equation from the displacements predicted by the network itself. Our approach generalises to previously unseen load cases and geometries, achieving easily convergence errors in the residuals of less than 1% and being capable of scaling up to models of considerable size and arbitrary geometries. To ensure compliance with the laws of physics and provide guarantees regarding the inference, it is possible to use the residual itself as an error indicator for the inference, and thus perform a refinement at the testing stage if the residual tolerance set in advance by the user is not met. Examples are provided to demonstrate the performance of the proposed method. This results in a method that avoids the costly process of obtaining, curating and storing high-fidelity synthetic data for training the neural network. Whilst this is not unique to our method, it is the first time it has been combined with a geometric machine learning technique capable of providing the necessary geometric bias to overcome the well-known difficulties of physics-informed neural networks.
item.dc:creator: Mikel M. Iparraguirre, Iciar Alfaro, David Gonzalez, Elias Cueto

item.title: Space--time formulation of geometrically exact beams
item.description: arXiv:2608.02146v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We formulate the dynamics of a straight-reference geometrically exact Cosserat beam as a directed world sheet in non-relativistic space--time. The centerline history is embedded in \(\mathbb R^4\), while absolute time remains prescribed and is not an additional mechanical degree of freedom. Spatial force and moment resultants and temporal linear and intrinsic angular momenta are combined into common space--time fluxes, so that spatial Neumann data and temporal inflow and outflow are represented by one co-normal boundary operator. A mixed configuration--momentum system is discretized by continuous tensor-product finite elements and stabilized by a future-directed Petrov--Galerkin perturbation. The resulting time-aligned \(Q_2/Q_2\) method requires one scalar stabilization parameter and retains the interior momentum trace as the free terminal outflow. The numerical study verifies the terminal flux treatment by an exact rigid-motion state, establishes monotone convergence for a smooth manufactured shear--bending solution, quantifies the pre-response--accuracy trade-off under delayed loading, and verifies covariance under constant superposed spatial rotations. The stabilization is not a proof of strict domain-of-dependence causality; it biases the global space-time approximation in the future direction and reduces the measured pre-activation response. A conservative extension to non-aligned simplex facets is also analyzed. Although this extension is consistent and locally conservative, continuous equal-order \(P_2/P_2\) simplex spaces exhibit strongly mesh- and orientation-dependent inverse amplification and do not show mesh-uniform stability. The aligned \(Q_2/Q_2\) discretization is therefore recommended as the practical realization of the formulation.
item.dc:creator: C. Hesch, E. Sahin

item.title: Elastoplastic inherent strain-based topology optimization for residual stress reduction in metal additive manufacturing
item.description: arXiv:2609.07337v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper proposes a topology optimization method for reducing the residual stress arising in the building process of metal additive manufacturing. First, a layer-by-layer process analysis model based on an elastoplastic inherent strain method is introduced. In this model, the incremental displacement is solved anew at each layer step, and the stress history is explicitly incorporated into the constitutive equation as the stress accumulated up to the previous step, which guarantees the stress continuity across layer interfaces without introducing activation strains. Next, the design sensitivity of this analysis model is derived based on the adjoint method. Taking the pair of the stress and the equivalent plastic strain as the state variables reduces the dependency between layer steps to a one-step recurrence, and the adjoint fields are constructed as a layer-by-layer reverse sweep that reuses the coefficient tensors obtained in the forward analysis. Consequently, the cost of the sensitivity analysis scales linearly with the number of layers and remains of the same order as that of the forward analysis. An optimization problem is then formulated based on the density method to minimize the P-norm of the residual stress at the completion of the building process under the volume and final-use compliance constraints, and the derived sensitivities are verified by comparison with central finite differences. Finally, the proposed method is demonstrated through two- and three-dimensional examples of residual stress minimization under a compliance constraint. The results clarify that, under the elastoplastic analysis, the maximum residual stress is bounded by the yield surface, and the optimization therefore reduces the extent of the yielded and plastic strain accumulating regions rather than the peak stress value.
item.dc:creator: Takao Miki (Osaka Research Institute of Industrial Science,Technology), Jike Han (Kyoto University), Kazuhiro Izui (Kyoto University), Shinji Nishiwaki (Kyoto University)

item.title: Topology optimization of multimaterial aircraft pylons using generalized shape function approach
item.description: arXiv:2609.27685v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: As the primary structural component connecting the engine to the wing or fuselage, an aircraft pylon requires optimized structural efficiency; this paper provides topology optimization of multimaterial pylons using the generalized shape function (gSF) approach. The gSF method uses $n$ natural-coordinate design variables per element to provide optimized designs up to $2^n$ distinct material phases while promoting close to discrete material layouts in conjunction with the density and formulated Heaviside projection filters. Pylon structural compliance is minimized subject to volume constraints. Exploiting the geometric features of a typical pylon structure, multimaterial evolution is performed on a corresponding 2D design domain representing the midplane, with up to 14 candidate materials. The optimized two-dimensional layout is then extruded to achieve the corresponding three-dimensional optimized pylon structure. The Method of Moving Asymptotes is employed to achieve the final design variables. The resulting convergence histories exhibit smooth and stable objective minimization. The results highlight the capability of the multimaterial topology optimization framework to effectively optimized aircraft pylons with multiple candidate materials, without requiring a considerable expansion of the design variable set.
item.dc:creator: Swagatam Islam Sarkar, Prabhat Kumar

item.title: TaiJi: State-Conditional Adaptive Combination of Machine-Learning and Physics-Based Global Weather Forecasts
item.description: arXiv:2609.31972v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Machine-learning weather models now rival or surpass operational numerical weather prediction (NWP), yet no single model dominates across variables, pressure levels, lead times, or regions, and the returns from ever-larger individual models are diminishing. We present TaiJi (after the yin-yang concept of complementary opposites), a spatiotemporal adaptive ensemble framework that recasts optimal model-weight combination as a learned prediction problem: a lightweight convolutional neural network, conditioned on the recent atmospheric state, predicts at every grid point and lead time affine combination weights and an additive residual for the constituent forecasts. The combiner is trained end-to-end over Pangu-Weather, GraphCast, FuXi, IFS-HRES, and the IFS-ENS ensemble mean, a hybrid set of ML and NWP constituents, at less than a tenth of the cost of training any of its ML constituents. Under the WeatherBench 2 protocol (2020 test year), TaiJi outperforms the strongest baseline in nearly every combination of the eight core variables, lead times up to 10 days and two skill metrics (RMSE and ACC), and this advantage extends to heavy-precipitation extremes. The same state-conditional principle transfers to tropical-cyclone track forecasting: by fusing constituent tracks rather than gridded fields, TaiJi-TC reduces track error relative to the equally weighted multi-model consensus at lead times up to 96 h, by about 10% at 36 h, halves the slow along-track bias shared by all constituents up to 60 h, and lowers landfall position error by 13-15% at 60-84 h. The learned weights vary coherently with latitude, season and lead time rather than following a fixed rule. TaiJi thus offers an inexpensive route to better global forecasts that builds on, rather than replaces, existing forecast models.
item.dc:creator: Jiale Wang, Yining Li, Guihua Wang

item.title: Solution Strategies for Dissolution-Driven Phase-Field Fracture in Geomaterials
item.description: arXiv:2610.38367v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Dissolution-driven fracture governs the long-term integrity of geological CO2 storage, geothermal reservoirs, and nuclear waste repositories. Modeling it requires solving strongly coupled mechanical, chemical, and phase-field equations. The solver choice controls their accuracy, cost, and convergence. This study investigates the role of solution strategies in dissolution-driven fracture in geomaterials. The coupled model is implemented in Abaqus user-element (UEL) subroutines, with all tangent blocks derived analytically. Five solvers are compared: (1) block-diagonal Newton monolithic, (2) BFGS quasi-Newton monolithic, (3) single-pass fully staggered, (4) single-pass partially staggered, and (5) hybrid multi-pass fully staggered. Performance is quantified by accuracy (errors in peak load, peak and failure displacements, and local CO2 concentration), cost (CPU and wall-clock times), and robustness, measured by new factors that assess convergence over the whole simulation and capture iteration spikes. The solvers are tested on mechanical and chemo-mechanical tension, shear, and multiple-crack benchmarks, including CO2 diffusivities raised up to a thousandfold. The results reveal a clear trade-off between accuracy, cost, and robustness. The quasi-Newton solver matches the Newton reference at a fraction of its cost but can fail under intense transport. The single-pass fully staggered solver is inexpensive and always completes, but its post-peak response depends strongly on the time step. The hybrid multi-pass solver also always completes, retains near-reference accuracy, and avoids iteration spikes at moderate cost. The partially staggered solver is the least robust. These findings guide practical selection: the single-pass staggered solver suits rapid screening, quasi-Newton offers accuracy when convergent, and hybrid multi-pass provides the best balance.
item.dc:creator: Maithah M. Alaleeli, Mohamed Elkhodbia, Mostafa E. Mobasher

item.title: Offline Materials Optimization with CliqueFlowmer
item.description: arXiv:2603.06082v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recent advances in deep learning inspired neural network-based approaches to computational materials discovery (CMD). A plethora of problems in this field involve finding materials that optimize a target property. Nevertheless, the increasingly popular generative modeling methods are ineffective at boldly exploring attractive regions of the materials space due to their maximum likelihood training. In this work, we offer an alternative CMD technique based on offline model-based optimization (MBO) that fuses direct optimization of a target material property into generation. To that end, we introduce a domain-specific model, dubbed CliqueFlowmer, that incorporates recent advances of clique-based MBO into transformer and flow generation. We validate this model's optimization abilities and show that materials it produces strongly outperform those from generative baselines. To support specialized materials discovery applications and broader interdisciplinary research, we release our code (https://github.com/znowu/CliqueFlowmer), model weights (https://huggingface.co/iamkuba/CliqueFlowmer), and an interactive demo (https://cliqueflowmer.znowu.workers.dev).
item.dc:creator: Jakub Grudzien Kuba, Benjamin Kurt Miller, Sergey Levine, Pieter Abbeel

item.title: Graph-Based Kirchhoff Modeling of Non-Ohmic Electron Transport in Self-Assembled Nanonecklace Networks
item.description: arXiv:2607.03698v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Gold nanonecklace networks exhibit non-Ohmic current--voltage I-V characteristics with a sharp conduction threshold, making them promising for sensing and transistor-like devices. However, their conduction has been understood largely empirically, because experiments cannot see how conduction evolves inside the network. To address this, we develop a graph-based Kirchhoff modeling framework that resolves these internal processes, tracking the potential and current of every junction. Although every active element conducts linearly, the model reproduces the non-Ohmic response $I \propto (V-V_T)^\zeta$. It also captures the experimentally observed effects of junction properties, network density, and voids, which lends confidence to its predicted internal states. These states show that the non-Ohmic response emerges from voltage-driven percolation. Conduction is governed by how junctions are connected rather than by how many are active, with the current scaling approximately as \(N^{2.3}\) while the number of active junctions grows only linearly. Contrary to the expectation that junction heterogeneity strengthens the nonlinear response, homogeneous junctions in a well-connected network produce the most abrupt and reproducible turn-on. Thus, each structural parameter acts as a distinct control knob. The mean junction characteristics set the threshold, junction uniformity sets the switching sharpness, and network density and voids set the connectivity and current. These relationships provide design rules for tailoring nanonecklace networks to a desired conduction behavior through synthesis and fabrication.
item.dc:creator: Obed Issakah, Md Khirul Alam Titu, Srivathsan Badrinarayanan, Ravi F. Saraf, Janghoon Ock

item.title: Global Parameter Identification and Uncertainty Quantification of reduced-order ADM1 using Maximum Likelihood Estimation and Bayesian Inference
item.description: arXiv:2610.19098v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Anaerobic digestion (AD) models can be challenging to calibrate against real data due to limited practical identifiability, data scarcity, and model complexity. Weighted least squares objective functions and gradient-based solvers using finite differences are often used in literature, but result in suboptimal parameter estimates and large uncertainty bands. This paper identifies the parameters of a reduced-order ADM1 by comparing the frameworks of maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) and Bayesian inference (BI), and quantifies uncertainties of parameters and outputs. Multirate experimental data are taken from a lab-scale AD reactor fed with agricultural substrates and operated at organic loading rates of 3$\,$g VS $\mathrm{m^{-3}d^{-1}}$. Global optima are found via global and gradient-based local search algorithms using forward sensitivities. Enhanced scatter search provides the best global search results. These are refined by the Gauss-Newton algorithm as the best local search, which delivers $R^2$ values of 0.95 for acetic acid and 0.77 for biogas production. BI yields substantially narrower uncertainty bands than MLE and avoids the need for a global search by incorporating prior knowledge about parameter distributions. The search space is captured efficiently by log10 scaling of parameters. Algorithmic details on its implications are provided. Despite a high-resolution lab-scale dataset, the ADM1-specific inhibition parameter $K_\mathrm{I,nh3}$ is practically not identifiable with MLE, and shows a low output sensitivity, whereas a parameter for the effective ion concentration shows superb practical identifiabilty at high confidence with both MLE and BI. The present work lays a scalable base for calibration of nonlinear AD models by providing reliable simulations. It thus advances model-based monitoring and control applications of multirate processes such as agricultural AD plants.
item.dc:creator: Simon Hellmann, Leander Lerch, Terrance Wilms, Moritz Reumsch\"ussel, Alberto Meola, F\'elix Delory, Steffi Knorn, Stefan Streif, S\"oren Weinrich
